findings.label: Device work is a minor fraction of measured latency in 11 of 15 timing workloads; their walltime is set by the host launch path
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary, AI_VECTOR_CORE task _gelu_and_mul_rows_kernel, one op per profile

evidence.metric: task duration range within one profile (min/max over 100 invocations)

findings.inference: For 00000 the 2.4 us device task cannot account for the 0.0530 ms eval latency, and for 00001 the 3.9 us task cannot account for 0.0959 ms, so >90% of those calls is non-device time. For 00010 the 39.2 us kernel is at most 41% of the 0.0950 ms call, so at least ~56 us per call is non-device even under full host/device overlap. This is consistent with the round-3 hypothesis that these shapes are charged for host-side launch work. The profiler cannot separate Python/host cost from stream idle time, so the exact split stays an inference; eval latency from the snapshot remains authoritative.

findings.label: The launch shortcut is ineffective exactly for the hidden_size=4096 plan (input width 8192, BLOCK=4096, 1 tile), whose constexpr key coincides with the hidden_size=8192 plan
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary block_num confirms grid expansion in the normal compiled path; host path itself is not covered by msprof
findings.inference: The device kernel is identical in cost class across the three plans (2.4-39.2 us, one fused op), yet eval latency splits the 15 timing workloads into ~0.051-0.055 ms (input widths 2048 and 16384) and 0.0950-0.0996 ms (all four small input-width-8192 workloads), while the large cases are device-bound and unchanged. The width-8192 group is precisely hidden_size=4096, whose plan is (BLOCK=4096, EVEN=True, tiles=1); the width-16384 group is hidden_size=8192, whose plan is (BLOCK=4096, EVEN=True, tiles=2). Because the Triton compile key contains the constexpr pair but not the grid, those two plans share one cache entry, so the install gate at main.py:244-256 (`fresh = set(cache) - known`, then `len(fresh) == 1`) finds nothing fresh whenever the other plan was compiled first and never populates `_LAUNCHER` for (bfloat16, 4096, device). Every later call for that shape then takes the `kernel[grid](...)` fallback near its round-2 cost. The remaining ~50 us even on the working path shows the shortcut removes only part of the host cost. This mechanism is not directly observable in a device report; it is the single source-level state shared between the two non-improving and improving groups and is falsifiable by the next experiment.

findings.label: 00012 is device-bound and scalar-heavy: 4096 programs of a 1024-element tile leave ~31% of AIV time in scalar work and only ~9% in MTE2
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary; pipe ratios not additive, physical bandwidth not calibrated
findings.inference: Its 0.15364 ms eval latency matches the 153.4 us device task, so host cost is fully hidden here and the device side is what makes this the only sub-1.0 workload. MTE2 at 9.2% and ~25.2 MB of logical traffic in 153.4 us (~164 GB/s effective) give no support for a bandwidth claim; the striking asymmetry versus 00010 (same kernel, 4096-element tile: vec 0.787, scalar 0.121) is that 00012 runs 4096 programs of a 1024-element tile, i.e. 4x less work per program, so per-program scalar/address work is charged 4x more often per element. Pipe ratios are marginal activity shares and are not a time decomposition, so this identifies where to look, not a proven cause.

findings.label: The largest workloads are vector-bound on the FP32 exact-erf expression, not memory-bound
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary; no Roofline calibration performed
findings.inference: Vector-active time is ~76% of AIV time and 13x the MTE2 share, so for the multi-million-element cases the limiting resource is the vector pipeline executing the FP32 erf path, and this is where any further gain on 00013/00014 must come from. Even so, that cannot be converted into a utilization number: the vector share is a marginal activity statistic, and no calibrated FLOP ceiling for erf was measured.

findings.label: One fused device kernel per invocation, with no cast or copy capsules
findings.backend_detail: msprof op_summary has one AI_VECTOR_CORE op type per profile

evidence.metric: operation_count / distinct op names in report
op names present in report (all invocations)

findings.inference: The five-kernel reference chain (three of them casts) has been collapsed to a single BF16-in/BF16-out vector kernel on every profiled workload, so the round-3 numbers are produced by the intended fused path and the remaining gap is not explained by leftover cast or copy tasks on the candidate side.

performance_interpretation: Round 3 raised geo_mean from 1.3226 to 1.8102 (+36.87%) and all 19 workloads passed. The evidence splits the 15 timing workloads into three regimes. (1) Eight workloads at ~0.051-0.055 ms (input widths 2048 and 16384) where device work is 2.4-3.9 us and the host shortcut is evidently active, giving ~50 us of residual per-call host cost. (2) Four workloads at 0.0950-0.0996 ms, all with input width 8192 (hidden_size=4096, BLOCK=4096, single tile), whose device work is 3.9-39.2 us, so they are still charged the pre-round-2 host path of ~92 us; the only source-level state these four share with a plan that did improve is the (BLOCK=4096, EVEN=True) compile key, which is why the `len(fresh)==1` install gate is the leading suspect rather than a device-side difference. (3) Three device-bound workloads 00012/00013/00014 (0.154/0.301/0.615 ms) whose eval latencies match their kernel times; 00014 is vector-bound on FP32 erf (76% vector share), while 00012 - the only sub-1.0 result at 0.903x - spends ~31% of AIV time in scalar work because its plan is 4096 programs of a 1024-element tile. So the dominant bound is mixed: host launch path for eleven workloads, vector compute for the two largest, and per-program scalar/vector efficiency for the one regression. No Roofline statement is made; pipe ratios are marginal activity shares, not a time decomposition.

next_experiment.action_description: Stop gating the launch-shortcut installation on a JIT-cache diff. In `gelu_and_mul`, use the CompiledKernel object returned by the normal `_gelu_and_mul_rows_kernel[grid](...)` invocation to populate `_LAUNCHER[(dtype, hidden_size, device)]` on the first call for that key, and delete the `known = set(cache)` / `len(fresh) == 1` gate (main.py:244-256). Include the plan (block, even) in the launcher key so a future plan change cannot reuse a stale handle, keep the `_shortcut_allowed()` profiler-hook guard and the try/except that drops the entry and falls back to the normal launch, and keep cached state metadata-only (no tensors, addresses or outputs).
next_experiment.expected_impact: All four width-8192 workloads (00001/00004/00007/00010) should move from 0.0950-0.0996 ms to roughly 0.051-0.060 ms, i.e. 1.30-1.36x -> ~2.2-2.5x, since their device tasks are only 3.9-39.2 us and the sibling plans already run at ~0.053 ms. Expected geo_mean 1.810 -> ~2.0-2.1 (+11% to +17%); the large device-bound cases should not move.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: If `JITFunction.run` does not return a usable CompiledKernel on FlagTree 0.6.0+ascend.gitc286cba6, installation must be skipped and the call must still execute the kernel exactly once (verify the compute is not launched twice, which would show up as two device tasks per iteration). Keep the generic-stride path and the profiler fallback untouched; profiling compatibility (launcher needing Tensor `size()` metadata) must not regress. Roll back to the current install logic if the four workloads do not reach the target latency or if any correctness workload changes.
success_criteria: Full eval reports PASSED with all four correctness workloads at matched_ratio 1.0 and unchanged tolerance.
Headline geo_mean >= 1.95 with no regression on 00000 (currently 0.0530 ms) or 00014 (0.615 ms).
Profiling still shows exactly one _gelu_and_mul_rows_kernel task per invocation, confirming no doubled launch and that the device kernel itself is unchanged.

warnings: msprof timing is diagnostic and is not eval latency; all speedups and latencies in this analysis come from the frozen evaluation snapshot.

Profiling installs launch hooks, so the shortcut guard may disable the fast path during collection; per-iteration gaps in the profiled run cannot be used to infer host cost or to confirm the shortcut state.
Pipe utilization ratios are marginal activity shares and do not sum to a time decomposition; no quantitative Roofline claim is made.
Instruction-level escalation was not requested because the device counters already separated the three regimes.
open_questions: The working host path still costs ~50 us per call even where the shortcut is active, versus the 17.9 us CPU-measured launcher cost; whether that residue is output allocation, plan/stride checks, or remaining launcher-side work is unmeasured (msprof has no host-side breakdown).

The constexpr-key collision is inferred from the source and the eval split; no artifact directly reports whether the shortcut was installed for a given shape. The next experiment falsifies or confirms it.

Whether 00012's 31% scalar share can be reduced by handling several rows per program (a 2D row-tile keeps the affine layout but cuts program count); the 1024-element row width caps a single-tile plan at BLOCK=1024.
Whether the reference's advantage on 00012 (0.903x) comes from PyTorch's vectorized erf path or simply from its element ordering; not separated by this round's data.
